Exact statement: Every nonnegative parallel mixture of N887 scalar suppression modes preserves the increasing-period ethane trend, opposite the duty10 grid. This conditionally rejects that shared family while preserving its valid single-waveform nonidentification theorem. Sensitivity thresholds do not acquire uncertainty or matched actual exposure. A fixed three-configuration mechanism reverses the sign but has poor quantitative fit. Sequential randomized scheduled-pulse omission plus fresh cohort/common read identifies a finite history-dependent effect without claiming global reset, subject to acquired recovery/exposure/background bounds and complete product/work costs. Dense terminal overshoot/charging and known prior withdrawal experiments prevent promotion to a new physical operation.

# Existing equal-duty grid tests the scalar witness family

## Result

The final Figure 2 source contains exact equal-duty pairs. Its point values are inconsistent with N887's **shared-fixed-rate scalar family** across those protocols, conditional on comparable calibrated molar-flow regimes. This does not refute the theorem about endpoints plus one mean, and does not exclude general slow hidden states. No statistical significance is claimed: the source supplies no replicate identities or error bounds for these grid values.

## Primary values and definitions

Source: publisher MOESM20 XLSX, freshly downloaded, SHA256 47a571bed2750c89ba2cf38cc75235f1e7497727c57e2b9b28fc3fdfc667a3fe.
https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41557-026-02107-8/MediaObjects/41557_2026_2107_MOESM20_ESM.xlsx

The two sheets report conversion and selectivity for the same 30-condition (6 by 5) duration grid, not separate duration sweeps. Sheet Figure 2 c columns B,C,D are t1.5V / s, t-0.1V / s, Conversion / %. Sheet Figure 2 d has the same B,C durations and D=Selectivity / %. The following four rows all have h/d=10, with the same commanded +1.5/-0.1 V levels:

Use the paper's branching definition S=a/(a+b), not conventional net selectivity. With X and S expressed as fractions and common molar-flow normalization, b/Ain=X(1/S−1). This is a conditional material-balance reconstruction, not native chromatogram-derived flux. No interpolation, mixing with preprint values, or use of the distinct Figure 2 b optimum row is involved.
